cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: The supplied paper.txt is an earlier working-paper version (564 subjects, one wave, 'Active Choice' naming), so the specification was taken from the claim descriptions together with the data's variable labels.

Controls coding is my choice: field of study as subject_cat dummies, high-school GPA as q_abitur_grade_cat dummies (the category for missing GPA keeps N=12160), last math grade as q_math_grade_cat quartile dummies, perceived multitasking as both perc_multitasking_1 (Likert) and perc_multitasking_2 (relative), payoff scheme as Treatment_Incentives dummies, wave as original_lab. Online controls are age, gender dummies, and window_height1 and window_width1 for screen size.
cell.notes: Attempt-1 was exploratory: it looked at variables and labels and printed no RESULT lines. Final run: the lab sample drops the Ample condition (Treatment_Incentives==4), which leaves 12160 subject-rounds and 608 subjects across Baseline, Directed Attention and Forced Choice. All models are OLS with fixest, SEs clustered by subject_id. Outcomes: summation_correct (decision task), default_followed (default adherence), load_correct (background task), payoff_share; online: memory in formatted_data_long_mturk.dta (5472 obs, 608 subjects). Every RESULT matches its claimed value to the reported precision. I compared after the final run and did not change the script afterwards, so there are no claim attempts. No docker hangs.
